steps.title: Chenin Blanc
steps.body: Swartland is famous for old-vine Chenin Blanc, from dry-farmed bush vines, some over 50 years old. The wines are concentrated, textured and mineral, with quince, stone fruit, honey and fresh acidity, often fermented in old barrels or concrete. Chenin is often blended with other white grapes, like Grenache Blanc, Clairette, Roussanne and Viognier, in Cape white blends.

steps.title: Syrah and Grenache
steps.body: Rhône grapes suit the heat and drought: Syrah gives peppery, savoury reds; Grenache gives red fruit and spice; Cinsault, light, fresh reds; Mourvèdre and Carignan add structure. Blends of these, inspired by the Rhône, are a Swartland signature. Sadie Family's Columella is a famous Syrah-led blend.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its style.
steps.explanation: Swartland mixes Chenin and Rhône grapes.

steps.body: Look for the Swartland Independent seal on the bottle. It marks wines made under the group's minimal-intervention rules.

steps.prompt: Which white grape is Swartland most famous for?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Old-vine Chenin Blanc is Swartland's white signature
Cape white blends mix Chenin with Rhône whites
Syrah, Grenache and Cinsault lead the reds
